issues.description: Method visibility mismatch for helper method singFarmSongVerse(Animal). The problem statement text instructs: "For easier testing, make sure to implement the helper method singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) as public." (problem_statement.md line 113). The UML in the same problem statement marks the method as private (a '-' visibility) in the Farm class (problem_statement.md line 19). Both the template implementation and the reference solution declare the method as private: template src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java defines the signature at line 18 as private void singFarmSongVerse(...), and solution src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java defines the signature at line 33 as private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). This contradiction between prose, UML and code can confuse students about the required visibility and may cause tests that expect a public helper method (for direct invocation) to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the visibility consistent across specification and code. Two acceptable fixes: (A) If automated tests require direct access to singFarmSongVerse, change the method declarations in the template and solution to public and update the UML to show '+' for the method. Modify src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java signature line (template line 18 and solution line 33) to: public void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). (B) If the helper is intended to be private, update the problem statement prose to remove the sentence that asks students to implement the helper as public (problem_statement.md line 113) so the textual instruction matches the UML and code. Prefer option A only if tests call the helper directly; otherwise prefer option B to keep the UML and code consistent with the text.
